literal: Weeping acquired all weeping will go; even if lost, later will yield things of good nature.
translation: All that is acquired by making others weep will depart, making oneself weep. But things of a good nature, even if lost, will yield benefits later.
modern: பிறர் அழும்படி தீய வழியில் சேர்த்தவை எல்லாம், தாமும் அழும்படி விட்டுப் போய்விடும். ஆனால் நல்ல வழியில் வந்தவை தற்காலிகமாக அழிந்தாலும், பின்பு நல்ல பலன்களையே தரும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts wealth gained through cruel means with wealth gained through righteous means. The word 'அழ' (weeping) is used twice to show a direct consequence: wealth acquired by causing tears will be lost in a way that brings tears to the acquirer. Conversely, 'நற்பாலவை' refers to things of a good, pure nature. Even if such good things are temporarily lost, they will eventually yield positive results.
